description: Eight 16-step gate rows on one clock, each row with its own start point, end point, mute and pattern-shifting buttons

params.text: Sets the rate of the internal clock, its value from -2 to 6 read as two to that power in hertz
Starts and stops all eight rows; they come up running
Sends every row back to its own Start step
Turns this step on or off for its row; a row's Gate output goes to 10V while the clock is high on a step that is on
Sets the step this row returns to after passing its End step; the knob counts from 0 while the panel numbers the columns from 1, so it reads one less than the column
Sets the last step this row plays before returning to its Start step; the knob counts from 0 while the panel numbers the columns from 1, so it reads one less than the column
Holds this row's Gate output at 0V while it is switched on; the row keeps stepping and its pattern is unchanged
Shifts this row's pattern one step to the left each time it is pressed, the step falling off the left end coming back in at the right
Shifts this row's pattern one step to the right each time it is pressed, the step falling off the right end coming back in at the left
Chooses what the nudge buttons move: the upper position, marked i, shifts only the steps between that row's Start and End, and the lower, marked a, shifts all 16

inputs.text: Added to the Clock knob before the rate is worked out, so one volt doubles the rate
Takes over the clock; each rising edge above 1V advances every row one step, and the Clock knob and CV input are ignored while a cable is here
Added to the Reset button, and a total above 1V sends every row back to its own Start step

outputs.text: 10V while the clock is high and this row's current step is on, and 0V otherwise; a muted row stays at 0V

notes: the module comes up running on its own clock; patch a clock to Trig to take it over.
a row whose End knob is set below its Start knob plays its Start step and nothing else.
the lamp behind each row's mute switch is lit while that row's Gate output is high, and the lamp in each step button shows whether the step is on, brightest on the step the row is playing.
randomising the module fills every row's step pattern at random and leaves the knobs, the mutes and the nudge mode switch untouched.
